FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: Changes are live; a restart restores the configured default.

FontString.name: $parentCatchUpText
FontString.text: Your party's level gaps are read from the group.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: Followers receive your Herbalism, Mining and Skinning values so they can work the same nodes and skin the same corpses, and they stay in step while you play: when your skill grows, theirs does. They are only ever raised, never lowered, so a character you played yourself keeps its own progress. Crafting professions and recipes are not copied: the leader keeps those.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: This server treats a bound item as bound to the party rather than to one character. With binding off, a soulbound piece can be traded, mailed, sold on the auction house and handed to a companion like any other item, and an enchant that would bind it does not stop it either. While the rule is off the soulbound bit is removed from carried items, so the client offers them in every trade window. Turning binding on restores the ordinary rule, where a bound item stays with the character that bound it.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: A multiplier on the drop chance of each quality: x4 turns a 20% blue into 80%, x6 turns a 3% legendary into 18%, and anything past 100% simply becomes a guaranteed drop. No extra rolls, no extra items, no duplicates, and poor and normal are never touched.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: A multiplier on the coin loot generates: creatures, chests, mines and containers. It does not touch vendoring, quest rewards, mail or the auction house.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: What a Warband supplier charges and pays: the item's original sell price times the multiplier for its quality, and never less than the floor. The same price is charged and paid, so nothing can be bought low and sold high. Press Apply prices to write them onto the items - the new prices appear in game after the worldserver restarts, and nothing is re-priced on its own.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: Every grey item the Warband loots is sold on the spot, so it never takes a bag slot, and the copper goes to whoever looted it. Quest items, quest-starting items and anything an accepted quest still needs are never sold, and a grey no vendor would pay for is left where it is. Followers sell too: their bags are the ones that fill up where nobody can empty them by hand. A bag that is already full cannot be emptied by looting, so use the button below or .warband trash sell.

Button.name: $parentSweep
Button.text: Sell the junk in our bags now

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: A creature killed inside a dungeon or raid stays dead for the run. The cleared corridor is remembered on disk, so leaving for a while, logging out or a server restart does not bring the trash back. An instance reset does: the client's Reset all instances, a GM reset, or the daily reset hour, which is what a reset is for. Open-world respawns are never touched.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: Open-world creatures, quest rewards and loot present at each character's own level. The switch turns the mod-zone-scaling module on or off; it does not create zones - the server's own zone list decides where scaling applies, and with the module's DefaultBehaviour = off an enabled module still changes nothing until a zone is opted in. Off is the shipped state, so the world plays exactly as the base game until you turn it on.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: Loot one corpse and the window also holds what the other nearby corpses carry - gold included - so a cleared pack is emptied from one place. Everything here is server-wide configuration for mod-aoe-loot; each character can additionally toggle it with .aoeloot on/off. Off is the shipped state, so the base game's one-corpse window stays the default until you turn it on.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: The random bots that wander the world are logged in and out by the playerbots module itself. They are ambience, not Warband: on a single-player server a party of five plays better with an empty world. Switching them off logs out the ones online right now; the target pins how many stay logged in. Your own companions are never random bots and are never touched. Both choices are written to the playerbots configuration, so they survive a restart.

FontString.name: $parentHint
FontString.text: Two timers a party of five cannot keep by hand. The hearthstone is ready again the moment it is used. A hunter pet's happiness drains on a timed tick and drops a step every time the pet dies, and a follower will never feed it, so every pet is kept at full happiness - the leader's included.
